title.text: A Unified Physics-Based Compact Model and Calibrated Circuit-Validation Flow for Multi-Material CFET Logic: Si, SiGe, MoS

author: M. Nisha Angeline
affiliation: Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Velalar College of Engineering and Technology, Thindal, Erode, Tamil Nadu, India (e-mail: nishavlsidesign@gmail.com)

runs.text: Complementary FET (CFET) stacking removes the n/p lateral separation from the standard-cell footprint, but the choice of channel material for the two tiers is still open. We present a unified, physics-based compact model (UCM-CFET) whose single equation core (EKV-type smooth overdrive, velocity-saturation-limited drift–diffusion current with a

drain-voltage interpolation, charge-conserving terminal charges, series resistance and temperature dependence) is extended by material blocks: quantum capacitance and trap-limited ideality for two-dimensional MoS
channels, a Landauer quasi-ballistic branch with a metallic-tube shunt for carbon-nanotube (CNT) arrays, and an electro-thermal node for GaN. Nine device models (Si GAA n/p, SiGe p, MoS

p, CNT n/p, GaN n and projected p-GaN) are written once as Verilog-A for Cadence Spectre/ADE, mirrored exactly (within 0.1%) by an open-source ngspice behavioural library, and calibrated by least squares to literature-anchored reference
data with 1.3–12.1% mean absolute percentage error on

families. The calibrated models drive a common CFET inverter cell with explicit inter-tier coupling capacitance, output parasitic and local-interconnect resistance, 5/7/9-stage ring oscillators (ROs), unified

and temperature sweeps, material-specific sensitivity studies and Monte Carlo yield analysis. At nominal supply the 5-stage ROs run at 19.39, 21.39, 2.59, 45.39 and 1.69 GHz for the Si, SiGe, TMD, CNT and GaN platforms with 2.09, 2.12, 0.67, 0.84 and 94.17 fJ per cycle. A contact-resistance crossover map shows the TMD CFET keeps an iso-frequency energy advantage over Si only below a critical contact resistance; the CNT inverter loses its gain once the metallic-tube fraction exceeds about

; the GaN platform shows a frequency temperature coefficient of 501 ppm/K between 300 and 500 K. The outcome is a material-selection map rather than a single winner, together with conceptual, DRC-clean GDSII layouts of the five inverter and RO cells.

The complementary FET (CFET), in which the p-channel device is stacked vertically over the n-channel device around a common gate, is the leading candidate to continue track-height scaling below the lateral gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet node [1, 2, 3]. Because the two tiers are fabricated sequentially or share a common stack, the CFET also opens the possibility of placing

in the two tiers: strained SiGe for the hole channel [4, 5], two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) for ultimate thickness scaling [6, 7, 8, 9, 10], aligned carbon-nanotube (CNT) arrays for quasi-ballistic transport [11, 12, 13], and wide-band-gap GaN for high-temperature or power-control logic [14, 15, 16, 17].

Assessing these options at the circuit level requires compact models that are (i) physically interpretable, so that a material parameter such as contact resistance or metallic-tube fraction maps to one model parameter, (ii) numerically smooth, so that Spectre or ngspice converge in ring-oscillator (RO) transients, (iii) charge-conserving, so that delay and energy are meaningful, and (iv) calibrated by a documented procedure. Industry-standard models such as BSIM-CMG [18] satisfy (ii)–(iii) for Si but do not expose 2D, CNT or GaN physics; published 2D [19] and CNT [20] models are material-specific and are rarely compared on one footing.

This paper makes four contributions. First, a unified compact model (UCM-CFET) with one core and four material blocks, written in Verilog-A for Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre/ADE [21, 22, 23] and mirrored by an ngspice behavioural library [24] that reproduces the Verilog-A equations to within 0.1%. Second, a reproducible calibration flow with explicit targets and error metrics. Third, a complete circuit-validation flow (inverter cell with CFET parasitics, VTC, transient delay and energy, 5/7/9-stage ROs,

and temperature sweeps, material-specific sensitivity studies, Monte Carlo yield), executed identically for all five platforms. Fourth, a material-selection map derived from those results. The platform maturity is stated explicitly (Table I): the Si and SiGe models are advanced-node, roadmap-relevant; the TMD and CNT models are emerging post-Si projections; the GaN model, in particular its p-channel device, is exploratory.

runs.text: No measured or TCAD data were available, so the calibration targets are literature-anchored synthetic reference curves: for each device the on-current, off-current, subthreshold slope and DIBL at the platform

EKV-type formulation with a fourth-order power-law drain-voltage smoothing and explicit series resistance; the UCM is then fitted to those curves. This makes the fit a real test of the model's functional form (the two formulations differ in their saturation behaviour and charge interpolation), while keeping the targets traceable to published ranges [27, 28, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 17, 14]. The flow accepts measured or TCAD CSV files with the same column layout as drop-in replacements.

runs.text: Fig. 18 condenses the results on five normalised axes, and Table VI states the resulting recommendations. No platform dominates. The CNT CFET has the highest speed and the second-lowest energy but needs a metallic-tube fraction below

and carries a 10% frequency spread from density variation. The TMD CFET has the lowest absolute energy per cycle and the lowest supply, but at equal frequency it beats Si only with contacts below 0.32 k

m per side, and its 34% frequency spread makes it the hardest platform to close timing on. The Si and SiGe CFETs are the reference: SiGe buys 6–10% speed and a balanced inverter at no energy cost and with the lowest variability of all platforms. The GaN CFET has the best temperature stability of the frequency (501 ppm/K) and keeps a functional inverter to 150

C, but with the projected p-GaN device it pays 1–2 orders of magnitude in energy per cycle and, within a subthreshold-only leakage model, does not out-leak Si at high temperature; it is the platform whose ranking depends most on a device (the p-channel) that does not yet exist in the required form.

runs.text: The reference data are literature-anchored reconstructions, not measurements; the MAPE values quantify the model's ability to follow an independent formulation, not agreement with hardware, and must be re-established with measured or TCAD curves before the models are used for a specific technology. The p-GaN device is a projection. The TMD block omits Schottky-barrier bias dependence of the contacts and the CNT block uses a single transmission parameter; the charge model uses a symmetric end-point partition rather than a full Ward–Dutton partition; CFET parasitics are lumped. The sensitivity and Monte Carlo trends, which are the main results, are driven by the physical parameters of the model and are therefore expected to be robust to these simplifications, but the absolute numbers should be read as platform-level projections.
A single compact-model core with four material blocks, implemented once in Verilog-A for Spectre/ADE and mirrored in ngspice, allows Si, SiGe, MoS

, CNT and GaN CFET logic to be calibrated, simulated and compared with one flow and one set of measurement definitions. The flow reproduces a 5-stage RO at 19.39 GHz and 2.09 fJ/cycle for the Si baseline and yields a material-selection map: SiGe for p/n balance, TMD for the lowest energy at low
provided the contact resistance stays below the crossover value, CNT for the highest speed provided the metallic-tube fraction stays below
, and GaN for high-temperature operation at an energy penalty set by the p-channel device. All models, scripts, layouts and results are released for reuse.
